name: July 16, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 16, 2024
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Peak called the meeting t0 order at 6:35 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer (arrived at 7:15 p.m.); Vice Chair Alicia Peak;
  Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb (arrived at 6:47 p.m.), Suzanne Guldimann, and Jake
  Lingo

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor; Loren Davis, Recreation
  Coordinator; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Chair Peak led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Guldimann seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0; Chair
  Skophammer (arrived at 7:15 p.m.) and Commissioner Goldfarb (arrived at 6:47
  p.m.) absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on July 12, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Social Media and Digital Marketing Presentation by Recreation Coordinator
  Loren Davis

  Recreation Coordinator Davis presented information on the Community Services
  Department's social media platforms and digital marketing efforts.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  Commissioner Guldimann stated the Community Services Department had a great
  social media presence.

  Commissioner Lingo suggested adding a quick response code to Linktree and park
  signs.

  Vice Chair Peak suggested creating a Department hashtag and incorporate it into
  social media posts.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 6:47 p.ml

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

. ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0; Chair Skophammer (arrived at 7: 1 5 pm.) absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 21, 2024 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting and the June l8, 2024 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and flle a report of activities, events,
  proj ects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in June 2024.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Malibu Community Pool Facility Rules
  Recommended Action: l) Review the Malibu Community Pool Facility Rules; and
  2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 16, 2024
  Page 3 of 5

  Commissioner Guldimann stated the rules should be prioritized by safety, with the
  most important rules listed first.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Manisco stated
  hypoxic training was extended underwater breath holding. She stated the practice
  is a safety concem for swimmers and lifeguards.

  Vice Chair Peak indicated agreement with Commissioner Guldimann and stated to
  list the rules starting with “No” first.

  Commissioner Guldimann suggested revising the rules that stated “are prohibited”
  to “No” to keep the language consistent.

  Chair Skophammer arrived at 7:15 p.m.

  Legacy Park Rehabilitation Proiect and Program Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Legacy Park rehabilitation
  project and outreach program.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated Legacy Park was beautiful, and the staff did a
  great job with the native gardens.

  Vice Chair Peak stated pollinator gardens would be a wonderful park addition and
  requested to partner with Webster Elementary School and provide students with
  educational opportunities at Legacy Park.

  In response to Vice Chair Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Recreation Supervisor Orosz was creating a Legacy Park docent program. She
  stated the Arts Commission wanted to provide art programs and events at the park.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Commissioner Guldimann stated the Legacy
  Park deed restrictions dictates the number of programs and events that could occur
  at the park.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated that each park parcel was allowed six
  Temporary Use Permits annually.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco stated July was Parks and Recreation month and
  Commissioners were provided a tote bag, a t-shirt, and bingo cards. She stated the
  Department has been promoting Parks and Recreation month on social media and
  banners were placed at City parks.
   Parks and Racreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 16, 2024
  Page 4 of 5

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided an update on Charmlee Wilderness Park
  maintenance, hikes, and the Equestrian Park.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that the ruts
  within Carmichael Road at Charmlee Wilderness Park were filled annually.

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on the Request for Qualifications
  for Aquatics Programs, Aquatics program enrollment, Day Camps, and Adult
  Softball.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated City staff
  teach swim lessons and aqua aerobics, and contract instructors teach water polo and
  swim team.

  Commissioner Lingo stated he could promote the Adult Softball Open Play
  program through the Malibu Little League database. He suggested promoting
  recreation programs at the Trancas Market Friday night concert series.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Lingo stated that Jessica Mark was interested in providing
  equestrian programs, but due to stables not being available, it would be challenging.

  Commissioner Goldfarb commended staff for their work and inquired if additional
  plant signage could be installed at Las Flores Creek Park.

  Vice Chair Peak thanked staff for assisting with the permitting and insurance
  issuance for the Point Dume Parade. She stated the Malibu Elementary School field
  should be opened on school holidays and suggested installing a sign at the school
  with weekend hours.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Skophammer adjourned the meeting at 7:46 p.m.
